questions.question: What is the value of(4 x²+9 y²+12 x y)/(144)?
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

(a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab

**Calculation:**

**(4 x²+9 y²+12 x y)/(144)**

⇒ **((2x)²+(3y)²+2times 2times 3times x y)/((12)²)**

⇒ **((2x+3y)²)/((12)²)**

⇒ **(((2x+3y))/(12))²**

⇒ ((2x)/(12)+(3y)/(12))²

⇒ ((x)/(6)+(y)/(4))²

**∴ Option 4 is the correct answer.**

questions.solution:

m = sec θ - tan θ

n = cosec θ + cot θ

**Calculation:**

m = sec θ - tan θ = (1 - sin θ)/cos θ

n = cosec θ + cot θ = (1 + cos θ)/ sin θ

m + n(m - 1) = m + nm - n)

(1 - sin θ)/cos θ + (1 - sin θ)/cos θ × (1 + cos θ)/ sin θ - (1 + cos θ)/ sin θ

(sin θ - cos θ - 1 + 1 - sin θ + cos θ - cos θ × sin θ)/sin θ × cos θ 

(- cos θ × sin θ)/sin θ × cos θ 

- 1

**∴ Option 4 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: An incircle with center O is drawn inside an equilateral triangle ABC and the length of the side is 12 cm. Find the area (in sq.cm) of the triangle which is not in the incircle.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Side of equilateral triangle = 12 cm

An incircle with center O is drawn inside an equilateral triangle ABC.

**Concept Used:**

Area of equilateral triangle = √3/4 × side²

Area of circle = πr²

Inradius of equilateral triangle = side/2√3

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/217efb580d95020302ae0e7c27b1ed25e532618b70dc9ee2118ca72ce15c3234.png] 

Given that the side length of the equilateral triangle is 12 cm, we can calculate the radius:

⇒ r = (12 / 2√3)

⇒ 6 /(√3)

⇒ 2√3 cm

Now, let's find the area of the incircle using the formula:

Area of incircle = π × r² 

Area of incircle = π × (2√3)²

⇒ 12π cm²

Next, we find the area of the equilateral triangle using the formula:

Area of equilateral triangle = (√3 / 4) × (side)²

Area of equilateral triangle = (√3 / 4) × (12)²

⇒ (√3 / 4) × 144

⇒ 36√3 cm²

Finally, we can subtract the area of the incircle from the area of the equilateral triangle to find the area outside the incircle:

Area outside incircle = Area of equilateral triangle - Area of incircle

⇒ 36√3 cm² - 12π cm²

⇒ 62.32 - 37.68

⇒ 24.64 cm²

**∴ Option 1 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: A milk merchant buys 30 litres of milk at the rate of Rs. 50 per litre and mixes 20 litres of water in it (water is free of cost).If he sells this mixture at the rate of Rs. 48 per litre, then what is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Quantity of milk purchased: 30 litres

Cost of milk per litre: Rs. 50

Quantity of water added: 20 litres

Selling price of the mixture: Rs. 48 per litre

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = Cost per litre × Quantity

Selling Price (SP) = Selling price per litre × Quantity

Profit = SP - CP

Profit Percentage = (Profit / CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

The cost price of 30 litres of milk = Rs. 50 × 30 = Rs. 1500.

He mixes 20 litres of water in it.

Total quantity of mixture = 30 + 20 = 50 litres.

The selling price of 50 litres of mixture = Rs. 48 × 50 = Rs. 2400.

Profit = Rs. (2400 - 1500) = Rs. 900.

Profit percentage = (900/1500) × 100 = 60%.

**Therefore, the profit percentage is 60%.**

P can fill a tank in 5 hours. Q can fill the same tank in 10 hours. R can empty the same tank in 20 hours. How much time will all the three take together to fill the same tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity (Total Work) = LCM(5, 10, 20) = 20 units.

Efficiency of P = 20 ÷ 5 = +4 units/hr

Efficiency of Q = 20 ÷ 10 = +2 units/hr

Efficiency of R = 20 ÷ 20 = −1 units/hr (negative work)

Combined efficiency = 4 + 2 − 1 = 5 units/hr

Time taken = Total Work ÷ Combined Efficiency = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipe P to fill the tank = 5 hours

Time taken by pipe Q to fill the tank = 10 hours

Time taken by pipe R to empty the tank = 20 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

Note: Work done by an emptying pipe is considered negative.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Efficiency of P, Q, and R working together = (+4) + (+2) + (−1)

⇒ Total Efficiency = 6 − 1 = 5 units/hour

⇒ Total time taken = Total Work ÷ Total Efficiency

⇒ Total time taken = 20 ÷ 5

⇒ Total time taken = 4 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns vs Time & Work

The underlying concept is exactly identical to standard Time & Work. The only difference is that an outlet pipe or a leak is assigned negative efficiency.

Combined Efficiency Rule

If two pipes A and B can fill a tank in x and y hours, and pipe C empties it in z hours, their combined 1-hour work = (1/x) + (1/y) − (1/z).

Tank Capacity Formula

If the absolute flow rate (liters/min or liters/hour) of any pipe is known, then Tank Capacity = Total filling/emptying time of that pipe × Flow rate.

questions.question: The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream is 8 : 3 and the boat can travel 22 km downstream in 24 minutes. Then, how much time will the boat take to cover 50 km upstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream is 8 : 3.

The boat can travel 22 km downstream in 24 minutes.

**Formula:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation:**

The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to the speed of the stream is 8 : 3. Let the speed of the boat in still water be 8x and the speed of the stream be 3x.

The boat can travel 22 km downstream in 24 minutes. The speed of the boat downstream is 22/24 = 11/12 km/min = 11/12 × 60 = 55 km/hr.

The speed of the boat downstream is 8x + 3x = 11x.

So, 11x = 55 km/hr

x = 5 km/hr

The speed of the boat in still water is 8x = 40 km/hr.

The speed of the boat upstream is 8x - 3x = 5x = 25 km/hr.

The time taken by the boat to cover 50 km upstream is 50/25 = 2 hours.

**Therefore, the boat will take 2 hours to cover 50 km upstream.**

questions.question: What is the sum of all three-digit numbers which are divisible by 15?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

We need to find the sum of all three-digit numbers divisible by 15.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of an arithmetic series: S = (n/2) × (first term + last term)

**Solution:**

To find the sum of all three-digit numbers divisible by 15, we need to determine the range of numbers and calculate their sum.

Find the first three-digit number divisible by 15.

The smallest three-digit number divisible by 15 is 105.

Find the last three-digit number divisible by 15.

The largest three-digit number divisible by 15 is 990.

Determine the number of terms in the series.

To find the number of terms in the series, we need to calculate the number of three-digit numbers divisible by 15.

The first three-digit number divisible by 15 is 105.

The last three-digit number divisible by 15 is 990.

Using the formula to find the number of terms:

Number of terms = ((last term - first term) / common difference) + 1

Number of terms = ((990 - 105)/15) + 1

Number of terms = (885/15) + 1

Number of terms = 59 + 1

Number of terms = 60

Step 4: Calculate the sum of the series.

Using the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series:

Sum = (number of terms/2) × (first term + last term)

Sum = (60/2) × (105 + 990)

Sum = 30 × 1095

Sum = 32,850

**Therefore, the sum of all three-digit numbers divisible by 15 is 32,850.**

questions.question: If the radius of the circle is 42 cm and the angle formed at the centre by an arc is 150°. What is the length of the corresponding arc ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The length of an arc is a direct fraction of the circle's total circumference.

Fraction of the circle = 150° ÷ 360° = 5/12

Total circumference = 2 × (22/7) × 42 = 264 cm

Length of the arc = (5/12) × 264 = 110 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 110 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (r) = 42 cm

Angle formed by the arc at the centre (θ) = 150°

**Formula Used:**

Length of arc = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

**Calculation:**

⇒ Length of arc = (150° ÷ 360°) × 2 × (22 / 7) × 42

⇒ Length of arc = (5 / 12) × 2 × 22 × 6

⇒ Length of arc = (5 / 12) × 264

⇒ Length of arc = 5 × 22

⇒ Length of arc = 110 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 110 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The area enclosed by an arc and two radii is called a sector. It is calculated using the formula: Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².

Circumference of a Circle

The total perimeter or boundary length of a complete circle is known as its circumference, given by the formula 2πr.

Arc vs Chord

An arc is a curved, continuous segment of the circle's outer edge, whereas a chord is a straight line drawn inside the circle connecting two points on its circumference.
